summary: Mid-market analytics SaaS building multi-tenant search & assist features. Currently on another LLM API provider (primary: OpenAI) and running into cost and latency variability at scale. Evaluating a move to Redwood Hosted for parity test and then Dedicated for committed capacity. Primary asks: prompt parity, deterministic fallbacks, VPC/KMS for PII, and predictable unit economics.

notes:
- POC notes: integrated Redwood Hosted using a thin compatibility shim to keep existing OpenAI-style calls.
- Positive: lower p50 latency variability; observed 18% cost reduction on average token spend in test workload.
- Negative: several prompts (multi-paragraph summarization and legal clause extraction) returned different phrasing leading to downstream NER failures — labeled 'parity-regressions'.
- SE Marcus ran a prompt-parity harness (1000 test prompts) — results saved in Drive. Key metric: semantic-similarity >= 0.92 for 78% of prompts; target 90%.
- Security: SOC2 in place, customer requests KMS integration for encryption at rest (bring-your-own-key), and SAML SSO for internal access to Console. Needs DPA/data-residency language for EU customers.
- Ops: Nimbus wants predictable throughput: target 200 qps for embeddings/short chat and 45 concurrent long-generation streams with p95 < 400ms for token streaming start. Dedicated sizing estimate under discussion.
- Quote: finance asking for committed discounted pricing vs pay-as-you-go; initial ARR estimate $150k/y for medium commit (subject to final sizing).
- Quote from product lead: "We need parity on tone + structure for legal summaries — small wording changes break our downstream classifiers."
- Risk: if parity can't be achieved with reasonable prompt engineering, migration will stall.
- Good signal: product team liked Redwood's model-switch routing and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants during load.
migration_notes:
- Strategy: two-phase migration. Phase 1: replace incumbent with Redwood Hosted behind compatibility shim, run parity harness + A/B for 6 weeks. Phase 2: move to Redwood Dedicated with pinned model versions and VPC peering when parity targets met.
- Compatibility shim: maps OpenAI-style params to Redwood SDK; preserves temperature, max_tokens, and function-calling formats. Minor mapping for stop sequences needed.
- Parity approach: combination of prompt engineering + eval harness + regression alerts (semantic-similarity + token-delta + downstream NER F1).
- Observed regressions: creative rephrasing causing classifier mismatches — plan is to use system-level constraints + few-shot examples to lock phrasing.
- Rollback plan: maintain routing policy that can fallback to incumbent provider per-customer if top-line quality drops below threshold during rollout.
poc_results:
- Duration: 4 weeks sandbox POC.
- Perf: p50 latency for short-chat 98ms hosted, p95 320ms. Incumbent p50 110ms, p95 760ms.
- Throughput: sustained 150 qps in hosted sandbox with batching; Dedicated projections 300 qps with 4x GPUs.
- Quality: semantic-similarity mean 0.89 vs incumbent baseline 0.93 (target 0.92).
- Cost: estimated token-unit cost ~18% lower in hosted tests; Dedicated expected to be ~35-45% lower at commit levels.
- Action items from POC: retune 6 critical prompts, run second harness, finalize Dedicated sizing and pricing.
